questions.q: "The server is down." Which two things can that mean?
options: The server program stopped, or the server machine is off/unreachable
It always means the internet is down
questions.explain: "Server" means both a program that answers requests and a machine that runs such programs. Say which one.

questions.q: In what order does a server program prepare to receive customers?
options: socket, bind (claim a port), listen, then accept (wait for a client)
questions.explain: accept() then sleeps until a client connects, and returns a new socket (a new file descriptor) for that client.

questions.q: You start Bazaar's server and get OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use. What does it mean?
options: Another program (often an old copy of yours) already listens on that port
Your code has a syntax error
questions.explain: Only one listener can own an address:port. Stop the other program, or use another port.

questions.q: Inside a container, a server is bound to 127.0.0.1:8000. Your laptop can't reach it. Why?
options: 127.0.0.1 accepts connections only from the same machine (here, the same container); use 0.0.0.0
questions.explain: 0.0.0.0 means all of the machine's addresses, so connections from outside the container can arrive.

questions.q: A server process can't accept new customers: [Errno 24] Too many open files. What ran out?
options: File descriptors: every open file AND every connection uses one
questions.explain: Close files and connections you open, and raise the limit (ulimit -n) for servers that truly need many.

questions.q: The load average is 16 on an 8-core server. What do customers notice?
options: Everything is slow: twice as many threads want a core as there are cores, so requests wait
questions.explain: Compare the load average with the core count (nproc). Above it, work queues up and latency grows.

questions.q: Most of Bazaar's web requests spend their time waiting for the database. What kind of work is that?
options: I/O-bound: it mostly waits for input/output
questions.explain: I/O-bound work benefits from threads or async (more waiting at once). CPU-bound work needs more cores or processes.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Bazaar promises 99.9% uptime. About how much downtime is that per month?
questions.explain: 0.1% of 30 days ≈ 43 minutes. 99.99% would be about 4.3 minutes; 99% about 7.2 hours.
